description: We're CosmoTI! A crew of IT and mechanical engineering students interested in space, coding, data science, AI, and turning ideas into projects. We enjoy figuring out how things work, experimenting, and learning together.
summary: Sentinela is a browser-based prototype for organizing crew health observations during long-duration space missions. Informed by NASA research on human-spaceflight health risks, it brings guided check-ins, reference ranges, personal baselines, trend charts, and an interactive body map into one interface. Crew members can review changes, see why an alert was raised, and find suggested next steps and supporting sources. Records are stored locally on the device, so routine check-ins and review do not require a live connection to Earth. Demo profiles and readings are simulated; thresholds are illustrative and have not been clinically validated. Sentinela supports crew awareness and discussion with onboard medical personnel. It is not a medical device, diagnostic system, or NASA service.
details:
Sentinela is a web prototype for astronaut health self-assessment and monitoring across different types and durations of space missions. Crew members complete guided check-ins to record health observations and review them through an interactive body map, trend charts, and alerts. NASA research on human-spaceflight health risks informed the indicators included in the prototype and the explanations linked to some alerts; the app does not retrieve health data from NASA.

The app compares readings with illustrative reference ranges and, when enough history is available, with the crew member’s personal baseline. Alerts explain what changed, why it may matter, suggest next steps, and link to supporting sources. Mission context can clarify some alert explanations, but does not change alert severity.

Sentinela helps crew members notice changes over time and organize their observations for discussion with onboard medical personnel. The prototype runs in a browser and stores records locally on the device. Readings are entered by the user; the app does not connect to NASA systems, medical devices, or wearable sensors.

Demo profiles and readings are simulated, and thresholds are illustrative, not clinically validated. Sentinela supports crew awareness and discussion. It is not a medical device, diagnostic system, or treatment tool.

We built Sentinela with React, TypeScript, and Vite. It uses React Router, i18next, Dexie with IndexedDB, Zustand, Recharts, and vite-plugin-pwa. Vitest is included for automated tests. The interactive body map, personal baselines, and source-linked alert explanations are central to the project’s approach.
